title: Taiwanese Drivers Will Soon Skip Tests in Parts of Australia
summaryZh: 澳洲多州將承認台灣駕照，免考即可換照，西澳與昆士蘭10月31日起實施。
summaryHi: ऑस्ट्रेलिया के कई राज्यों में ताइवानी लाइसेंस बिना टेस्ट के मान्य होंगे।
summaryEs: Varios estados australianos reconocerán el carné de conducir taiwanés sin examen.
summaryJa: 豪州の一部の州で、台湾の運転免許が試験なしで切り替え可能に。
summaryKo: 호주 일부 주에서 대만 운전면허를 시험 없이 인정한다.
summaryEn: Several Australian states will accept Taiwanese driving licences without new tests.
paragraphs: Taiwanese nationals will soon be able to obtain a driving licence in several Australian states without sitting a driving test, Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) announced on Tuesday.
The change follows Australia's decision in late July to recognise licences issued in Taiwan and 11 other countries, a move that should make settling in far easier for Taiwanese residents.

The rollout will be gradual. Western Australia and Queensland will introduce the arrangement on October 31, followed by South Australia, New South Wales and the Northern Territory in January 2027 and Tasmania the following month. Victoria and the Australian Capital Territory have yet to set dates.
Austroads, the body that brings together Australia's road agencies, said recognition was expected to begin in late 2026. The rules, however, will not cover temporary visitors.

Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung said MOFA was working with the Ministry of Transportation and Communications on a reciprocal policy, which would allow Australian drivers in Taiwan to enjoy similar treatment.
Good news for Taiwanese people in Australia! Soon they can get an Australian driving licence without taking a driving test.
Taiwan's foreign ministry shared the news on Tuesday. In July, Australia said it will accept licences from Taiwan and 11 other countries.

Western Australia and Queensland start first, on October 31. South Australia, New South Wales and the Northern Territory start in January 2027. Tasmania starts in February 2027. Two other places have not said a date yet.
This change is not for tourists. It is for people who live in Australia.
Taiwan's foreign minister, Lin Chia-lung, said Taiwan also wants to make it easy for Australian drivers in Taiwan.
Taiwanese people who move to Australia will soon be able to get a local driving licence without taking a test in several states, Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said on Tuesday.
The news follows an announcement by Australia in late July. It said it would recognise driving licences from Taiwan and 11 other countries.

Each state is starting at a different time. Western Australia and Queensland will begin on October 31. South Australia, New South Wales and the Northern Territory will follow in January 2027, and Tasmania in February 2027. Victoria and the Australian Capital Territory have not yet given a date.
The new rule does not apply to short-term visitors such as tourists. It is for people who live and work in Australia.

Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung said his ministry was working with Taiwan's transport ministry on a similar plan, so that Australian drivers living in Taiwan could also exchange their licences more easily.
Taiwanese nationals will soon be able to obtain a driving licence in several Australian states without sitting a driving test, Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) announced on Tuesday.
The change follows Australia's decision in late July to recognise licences issued in Taiwan and 11 other countries, a move that should make settling in far easier for Taiwanese residents.

The rollout will be gradual. Western Australia and Queensland will introduce the arrangement on October 31, followed by South Australia, New South Wales and the Northern Territory in January 2027 and Tasmania the following month. Victoria and the Australian Capital Territory have yet to set dates.
Austroads, the body that brings together Australia's road agencies, said recognition was expected to begin in late 2026. The rules, however, will not cover temporary visitors.

Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung said MOFA was working with the Ministry of Transportation and Communications on a reciprocal policy, which would allow Australian drivers in Taiwan to enjoy similar treatment.
Taiwanese nationals relocating to Australia will shortly be spared the need to retake a driving test in several states, Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) said on Tuesday.

The development stems from Canberra's announcement in late July that it would formally recognise licences from Taiwan and 11 other jurisdictions, removing a practical obstacle that has long frustrated newcomers.

Implementation is being staggered across the federation. Western Australia and Queensland will lead the way on October 31, with South Australia, New South Wales and the Northern Territory following in January 2027 and Tasmania a month later. Victoria and the Australian Capital Territory have yet to commit to a timetable.
Austroads, the umbrella organisation for Australia's road authorities, had indicated that recognition would commence in late 2026. Notably, the arrangement excludes temporary visitors.

Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung said his ministry was collaborating with the transport ministry on a reciprocal scheme, so that Australian drivers residing in Taiwan would receive comparable treatment.

Taiwanese nationals settling in Australia will soon be exempt from retaking a driving test in a number of states, according to an announcement by Taiwan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) on Tuesday.

The policy shift derives from Australia's decision in late July to recognise licences issued by Taiwan and 11 other jurisdictions. For many migrants, the requirement to pass a fresh test has represented a costly and time-consuming barrier to employment and everyday mobility.

Implementation will be phased. Western Australia and Queensland are scheduled to adopt the arrangement on October 31, while South Australia, New South Wales and the Northern Territory will follow in January 2027, with Tasmania joining in February. Victoria and the Australian Capital Territory have not yet specified a timeframe.

Austroads, the national association of road transport agencies, had anticipated that recognition would commence in late 2026. It is worth noting, however, that the scheme does not extend to temporary visitors.

Meanwhile, Foreign Minister Lin Chia-lung stated that MOFA was cooperating with the transport ministry on a reciprocal policy, ensuring that Australian drivers resident in Taiwan would ultimately benefit from equivalent treatment.
